Hi Maria —

Great to kick this off. Thanks for choosing Redwood for the Clarion pilot. To make the initial tenant setup as smooth as possible, here are the outcomes we want to lock in this week:

- Confirm admin roster for tenant/project invites (who should receive Owner/Admin roles).
- Decide project naming convention and service-account naming (we recommend: clarion-prod, clarion-staging, clarion-svc-seed).
- Determine API key strategy: per-service-account ephemeral keys vs. long-lived service keys behind KMS.
- Any networking constraints (VPC peering, egress IP allowlist) and KMS/HSM provider details.
- Target date for seed run and first smoke test.

Can you confirm the Clarion admin emails and whether the infra group should receive service-account docs? If helpful I can propose a tight 30-minute discovery slot today or tomorrow to capture these items and hand off to our implementations team (Marcus & Monica).

Attachments: I have a short checklist I can share in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Sofia

Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — copying Marcus for technical handoff. I've attached a concise onboarding checklist (see attachment) and written notes below for the key provisioning steps Redwood will take and the items we need from Clarion: 

Summary of Redwood steps (implementation):
- Create workspace and two projects: clarion-staging, clarion-prod.
- Seed a service-account in each project and generate an ephemeral API key for smoke tests. Keys are rotatable via the Console/API.
- If you bring your KMS, we configure envelope encryption integration and record KMS key ARN.
- Apply role mappings: Owner = tenant admins, ProjectAdmin = deploy engineers, Service = svc accounts (least privilege).
- Enable prefix KV caching for the seed workload to avoid early throttling.

Items needed from Clarion:
- Final admin list (emails) for Owner role.
- KMS ARN and any IAM role we should assume (if you want Redwood to write keys).
- Network allowlist for egress IPs (we'll provide a short list).
- Preferred project naming if different from our suggestion.

Procurement / SLA note:
- We typically accept a signed SOW + PO. I see procurement is looped in — happy to share our standard one-pager and the SLA ack.

Attachments included: clarion_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, redwood_api_key_rotation.md, doc_template_invite_email.txt

Proposed next step: 30-min implementation sync at 1:30pm PT today — does that work for your infra team?

Thanks,
Monica

Hi Maria and Clarion infra —

Short technical notes and a seed script attached to make the handoff reproducible. Key points: 

1) Service-account seeding pattern (recommended):
- Create service account with least privilege role: role:project.service-call.
- Use the Redwood Console to 'seed' and obtain a one-time API token for the smoke run.
- Sample Curl to exchange seed token for an API key (replace values):

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/clarion-prod/service-accounts/seed-token
    -H "Authorization: Bearer SEED_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER"
    -d '{"duration_seconds":3600}'

2) KMS note: Redwood supports envelope encryption using customer KMS (AWS KMS supported). We only store encrypted blobs; the KMS key ARN must be provided and an IAM role with decrypt permissions created in your account if you want Redwood to rotate wrapped keys.

3) API key rotation & ops:
- We'll set default rotation to 90 days for non-prod and 30 days for prod service keys. You can override via policy.
- We'll provide a webhook for rotation events to your infra team.

4) Network: I'll follow up with the egress IP list; we have a short set of IPs for US regions.

Attachment: service-account-seed-script.sh (bash, safe for infra to run in staging).

Proposed time for the smoke run: Monday 2029-09-23 at 10:00am PT. If that works, I'll schedule a 45-min window and include runbook steps.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
